headline: Profit jumps on a one-time gain; core growth stays strong
summary_short: Northern Trust posted diluted EPS of $4.23, up from $2.71 in Q1 2026 and $2.13 a year ago, as net income rose to $792.2M including a $525.4M pre-tax gain from the Visa Exchange Offer.
summary_long: Diluted EPS of $4.23 (+56% q/q, +98% y/y) and net income of $792.2M (+51% q/q, +88% y/y) were lifted by $451.5M of pre-tax notable items: a $525.4M gain from Northern Trust's second Visa Exchange Offer participation, partly offset by a $73.9M loss on repositioned AFS securities. Trust and servicing fees rose 1% q/q and 10% y/y on higher AUC/A and AUM from favorable markets and net inflows. FTE net interest margin expanded to 1.81% (+6bps q/q, +12bps y/y) on lower funding costs. Noninterest expense rose 9% q/q on $51.0M severance and a $33.1M one-time equity grant. CET1 ratio was 12.2%; the Corporation returned $499.4M to shareholders and raised its quarterly dividend 10% to $0.88.

drivers.explanation: Results were driven by $451.5M of pre-tax notable items (Visa Exchange Offer gain, partly offset by an AFS-securities repositioning loss); the CEO states ex-notable-items EPS grew 40% y/y.
Custody/fund administration and investment management fees rose from favorable markets and net new business/client inflows; AUC/A and AUM both grew double digits y/y.
Lifted by the $525.4M Visa Exchange Offer gain in Other Operating Income, partly offset by a $73.9M AFS-securities loss and higher noninterest expense.
EPS growth outpaces net income growth because the diluted share count fell alongside net income gains from the Visa-related notable items.
Equity growth reflects $792.2M of net income this quarter outweighing the $499.4M returned to shareholders via dividends and buybacks.
The Corporation repurchased 2,129,047 shares of common stock this quarter at a total cost of $350.6 million, reducing the diluted share count.
